findings.evidence: Lines 174 and 186 use `simp only [colorSingletState, ...]` to unfold the body in-file; no `colorSingletState_*` equation lemma exists (`grep colorSingletState` returns only lines 41, 51-52, 167, 170-171, 174, 182-183, 186). Compare `colorSingletProj_apply := (rfl)` at line 88, which the author did provide for the projector.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem colorSingletState_def : colorSingletState N = (((√N)⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • (1 : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) := (rfl)`, an entrywise `colorSingletState_apply`, and `@[simp] theorem conjTranspose_colorSingletState : (colorSingletState N)ᴴ = colorSingletState N`.
findings.issue: `colorSingletState` is public but has no equation lemma, and the section is `public section` without `@[expose]` (line 69), so downstream the state is opaque: a consumer cannot prove `colorSingletState N = ((√N)⁻¹ : ℝ) • 1`, cannot compute an entry, and cannot simplify the `(colorSingletState N)ᴴ` that appears in both exported lemmas (lines 171, 183).

findings.evidence: Line 264 of this very file does the unfolding by hand: `rw [casimir_genM_apply, colorOctetProj_eq, LinearMap.smul_apply, LinearMap.sub_apply, Module.End.one_apply, colorSingletProj_apply]`.
findings.fix: Rename the sum form to `colorOctetProj_apply_eq_sum` and add `@[simp] theorem colorOctetProj_apply (ψ) : colorOctetProj N ψ = ψ - ((N : ℂ)⁻¹ * ψ.trace) • 1`, parallel to `colorSingletProj_apply`.
findings.issue: There is no closed form for `colorOctetProj N ψ`. `colorOctetProj_apply` gives only the generator sum and is not `@[simp]`, and `colorOctetProj_eq` is operator-level, so applying the octet projector to a state requires a four-step rewrite while `colorSingletProj_apply` is simp.

findings.evidence: The file exposes only idempotency, orthogonality, completeness, traces and Casimir values; nothing relates a channel to the traceless/scalar matrices. Roadmap README.md:525-526: the colour/spin classification 'is the index set of every sum in Layer 2'.
findings.fix: Add `colorOctetProj_apply_eq_self_iff [NeZero N] (ψ) : colorOctetProj N ψ = ψ ↔ ψ.trace = 0` and `colorSingletProj_apply_eq_self_iff [NeZero N] (ψ) : colorSingletProj N ψ = ψ ↔ ∃ c : ℂ, ψ = c • 1`.
findings.issue: No lemma characterises membership of either channel, so a consumer cannot say which wave functions are singlet or octet — the content that Layer 2's channel-indexed sums rest on.

findings.evidence: `mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/OfAssociative.lean:49-50` declares `@[instance_reducible] def ofAssociativeRing`, enabled only file-locally (lines 66, 177); line 215 here does the same, and the docstring at lines 43-44 and 209-213 presents `LieAlgebra.ad ℂ _ X` / `LieModule.casimir ℂ _ _ (genM N) (genM N)` as the public vocabulary with no such note.
findings.fix: State in the `### The colour action on the pair` docstring that consumers must write `attribute [local instance 100] LieRing.ofAssociativeRing`, or additionally expose bracket-free restatements (e.g. the Casimir result as a plain matrix sum).
findings.issue: The colour-action and Casimir API (`ad_mul_colorSingletProj`, `colorSingletProj_mul_ad`, `commute_ad_*`, `casimir_genM_*`) is stated using a Lie structure supplied by a *local* attribute, and nothing in the public docstring says so; a downstream file cannot state or `simp` with these lemmas until it repeats the attribute, since the instance is not global.

summary: The projector surface is close to complete, but `colorSingletState` is exported with no equation lemma at all (body unexposed), the octet projector has no closed-form apply lemma, the two channels have no membership characterisation, and the closed-form trace results are missing `@[simp]`.
